records.c: Bytes ahead of the $0810 Speed entry. The instruction fragment calls $E5A0, blanks the VIC display and reads the CIA2 direction bits.
Blanks the display and clears $CE28 and $CE29. Restores the ROM mapping, selects VIC bank $8000, sets multicolour mode and initializes the sound routine with A=1 while the KERNAL is banked out.
Selects RAM under the KERNAL and copies five pages from $EB00–$EFFF into $C900–$CDFF. Jumps to the new code at $C900.
Waits for raster line zero before writing zero to $D011.
Waits for raster line zero and sets $D011 to $3B to enable the bitmap display.
Clears 94 bytes of the speed state at $C47C and seeds individual fields starting at $C4D9. Sets $1DE3 to $F8 and passes A=1 to the sound player.
Counts ten successful reads of VIC raster line zero before polling CIA1 port A for a new $6F match. Uses $CE23 as the held-press latch.
Two output screen digits updated by the award formatter at $0C6B. Both start at character $30.
Doubles the supplied sequence number and reads its pointer from $CC41. Passes each message ID to the positioned text routine until $FF.

Reads the column and row from a message selected through $CC5C, adds the row offset and uses $A400 as the screen base. $FE begins another positioned row, $FF ends the message and character values of $40 or above lose $40 before the store.

Clears the instruction matrix, copies seven resident 20-character rows and inserts the active apprentice’s name. Enables the character display, waits for fire and restores the gameplay matrix selection.
Fills $A400 through $A7FF with screen code zero.
Selects $A400 with character memory at $A000. Installs the three-page font from $FA00 and writes colour RAM using thresholds on the screen character codes.
Selects the $A400 screen matrix and copies font bytes from $FA00-$FCFF to $A000 while BASIC ROM is out. Sets colour RAM from the screen matrix before enabling character mode and waiting for fire.

Keeps one joystick sample in $C4B6 and selects movement sequences from exact active-low port values. A fire-only press flips the facing flag on release if the stick never combined fire with direction.
Selects a move stream from the pointer table at $C9B5. Control byte $C8 waits for a change of stick sample, and $CC tests whether the original sample is still held before advancing or cancelling.
Advances the animation counter when $C480 is armed. The selected pose is streamed into an inactive buffer in four 96-byte pieces before the displacement and sprite pointers are updated.

After three skipped calls, clears the line length at $C4AC and moves the line index at $C4DC one step toward $1C. Saves the preceding index in $C4C3 for erasing the old line. At the centre index it clears the recenter flag at $C49D.

Saves the old line index and accumulates a signed distance correction. When the accumulator passes the update test, advances the index by the signed step at $C4A8. Patches the comparison bounds from line length, reverses the step at a matching bound and may set either end flag.
Uses the old line index at $C4C3 to locate a generated line record through $C8B5. Walks the entries backwards and removes each saved pixel bit from the bitmap.
Uses the new line index at $C4DC to select the generated line record and OR its masks into the bitmap. Reads the corresponding position from the table at $C5CF for the ball sprite.

Toggles the water-edge selector at $C4C1. One side starts at $185C and the other at $18EC. Each selects either a frame from the water-edge tables or the open-column graphics when the respective progress value reaches six.
Reads left-hand progress at $C48F. Uses the source frame and reverse-order row strip for progress below six. At six or more it installs the $5D00 strips and clears lower cells.
Return byte after the unconditional jump at $1926. That jump enters the column clearer, whose own return exits the water update.
Resolves the selected column and horizontal strip sources through $C951 and $C961, then copies the left-side frame into the visible bitmap.
Writes eight bytes per cell down the bitmap, advancing the destination by one 320-byte row. Copies a final partial cell and zeros its unused rows before passing to the column clearer.
Zeros eight raster bytes per bitmap cell while advancing by 320 bytes, until the cell counter at $C4D5 reaches nine.
Writes the selected sixteen-pixel-byte strip in reverse order into $B280–$B28F.
Writes the selected sixteen-byte strip in reverse order into $B1B0–$B1BF.
Enables all eight sprites in multicolour, sets the X high bits for sprites four through seven, and assigns the shared colours.
Fills all four colour RAM pages with $0B for the speed playfield.
Copies 21 pages from $6000–$74FF to the visible bitmap at $A000–$B4FF. Then stamps selected colour cells with $E6.
Selects RAM under the KERNAL, enables the VIC raster IRQ, masks CIA1 IRQs and installs $1C09 in the hardware vector.
Acknowledges the raster interrupt, saves A, X and Y and advances $C4D4 through the three raster phases.
Installs six sprite pointers, position pairs and colours from the Speed state and display tables. Sets the next compare to $B3.
Positions eight sprites in two rows with fixed shape pointers and takes the next interrupt at $B7.
Advances the water timer using the state at $C4BF. Depending on that state it reaches the rise update at count $4B or $7D. The rise decrements the immediate operand at $1DE3 until it reaches $BA.
Polls the raster while reassigning sprite pointers and Y positions on lines $D0 and $E7. Uses the operand at $1DE3 as a raster threshold and cycles the four $D016 values at $C4E7.
Finishes the water phase and updates the sprite display using one of two gameplay paths. Writes the top sprite pointers and positions, sets the main-loop flag and schedules the next compare at $6E.
Reloads the endpoint and length from $C4CE–$C4D0 and rebuilds the current bitmap line through $C30A. Sets $C4DE when the call returns.

Authored gameplay bitmap pixels for rows 22–24 of the 40-column VIC matrix. The initial 21-page bitmap copy ends before this range.
Small pixel pattern after the 25 visible bitmap rows, before the standalone preview header.
Retained BASIC header with SYS 2070 and a JEDI text fragment. The preview program immediately follows.
Retained preview instructions following the Speed bitmap. They copy the image and configure the VIC bank, bitmap, colour registers and border in a display hold loop.
The retained $33 byte in the otherwise zero space just before the line generator at $C1E0. The slot directory and line geometry are later in memory.
Selects the next destination slot from the pointer table at $C8B5. Updates the source position and direction, reads a three-byte endpoint record and generates the addressed pixel masks for that line.
Forms the packed bitmap byte address and pixel mask from the line step coordinates. Writes each record as two address bytes followed by one mask.
Computes signed horizontal and vertical deltas from the supplied endpoint. Uses an integer error accumulator to step between the endpoints and passes each pixel to $C285.
Progress and rendering work bytes. $09F2 clears these 94 bytes before setting initial animation, joystick, water, line and result state.
Initial water cell and pixel counts, line index and step, current redraw state, and result adjustment fields. $09F2 installs the gameplay starting settings here.
Four $D016 values alternated by the water raster service at $1E09. The low three bits cycle horizontal fine scroll 1, 2, 3, 2.
Fifty-five repetitions of the same four $D016 values. The raster routine resets its index before fetching a fifth value.
Eight single-bit masks in the order selected by the bitmap line walker at $C2E0.

Three pairs of 16-bit coordinates per 12-byte group. $C1E0 advances the base by 12 and uses the first coordinates to generate a bitmap line. $17B0 uses the same line index to place the ball sprite. A final four-byte pair follows the full groups.
Sixteen little-endian bitmap addresses arranged in four rows and four columns. The row step is $140 and the adjacent columns differ by $18 or $20.
Per-sprite coordinate bytes, including the animated overlay and suspended ball positions. The pose and line routines write them before the raster handler places the sprites.
Fifty-five pointers to 180-byte slots for generated line records. Slots span ordinary RAM at $9000, RAM under I/O at $D000 and RAM under the KERNAL at $F000.
Eight further $B4-spaced addresses from $F924 through $FE10. The chamber initializer stops after 55 generated records before consuming this tail.
Fifteen little-endian offsets from zero through $A8, increasing by the 12-byte size of a line geometry group.

Retained copy of the Strength effect-driver bytes. Jumps to the voice dispatcher at $E02E.
Retained copy of the Strength effect-driver bytes. Sets the SID volume and mode to $1F. Clears the 24 voice and filter registers at $D400–$D417.

Retained copy of the Strength effect-driver bytes. A zero effect number disables the voice’s envelope and sets its test bit. For an active effect the low seven bits select a stream. The high bit requests a restart with the voice gate reset and the stream position reset to zero.
Retained copy of the Strength effect decoder. Its command bits control envelope, oscillator and voice-zero filter fields, then update the voice duration or clear the effect request.

Retained copy of the Strength effect-driver bytes. Steps frequency, waveform and pulse while the current duration runs. The frequency stream can set its high byte with $81 or redirect to a stream offset with another negative command. The waveform table maps indices to SID control bytes.
Retained effect voice stepper. Its ending SID cutoff store is interrupted by the Speed music entry at $E170.
The Speed music service entry jumps to the voice updater at $E222.
Clears the voice and filter state and resets the SID. Uses A to select the divider and six initial voice pointer bytes, and marks the first pass to fetch a sequence entry.
Interprets track bytes as a new track pointer, voice offsets or a repeat count. Nonnegative values select a phrase through the directory. Saves the new track position and begins the phrase.
Starts the player at voice index two or continues the current voice. The tick divider and note timers decide whether to fetch another phrase byte or step the instrument and write the active voice.
Selects the phrase using the current voice’s index. Decodes note, duration, instrument, filter, pitch override and slide commands. A zero byte returns to track processing.
Updates SID gate and envelope according to the instrument flags, resets modulation on a new note and reads the note frequency from its two byte tables. Updates the duration and saved phrase position.

Services the remaining voices by descending register index. The final voice updates the tick divider and SID mode and resonance. The filter step path reads a timed incremental cutoff command and writes $D416.

Initializes the slide when its counter is negative. Computes the interval from the difference of two note frequencies divided by the duration. Thereafter decrements the counter and adds the stored interval.
Writes a relative note lookup or a literal high frequency byte, then resumes instrument decoding. The silent branch resets the selected voice control and both envelope registers before moving on.
Uses the current instrument or the active override to select a pitch program. Applies its loop and timing fields and updates the note frequency from the program’s command.
Uses the instrument to choose a timed pulse increment program and advances that program when the countdown elapses. Adds the active increment to the saved pulse width.
Selects a fixed instrument control byte or the next byte from a control program. Applies the current voice mask and saves the program position.

Writes control, frequency, pulse width, attack/decay and sustain/release to the selected SID voice, then advances to the next voice. The Speed variant can write a zero sustain/release byte or skip its envelope write when the voice and gate checks suppress the normal path.
Sixteen eight-byte instrument records. The player reads the waveform settings, envelope, modulation and gate flags by using the selected instrument number times eight.
Split pitch program pointers and their loop controls, selected by the instrument or overwritten at index zero by an override.
Pulse, control and filter program pointers. The driver selects a program by the current instrument or filter command.
Pitch override directory, including split pointers, loop fields and the short programs addressed by those pointers.
Low bytes of the 95 SID note frequencies, paired with the table at $E802.
High frequency bytes referenced with the same note index as the low bytes at $E7A3.
SID register offsets 0, 7 and 14 for the three voices.
Voice and filter state initialized by $E173. Holds frequency, instrument, modulation positions, note counters and current track pointers.
Ten little-endian phrase pointers, read at twice the phrase number.
Two six-byte records. Each provides three track address low bytes and three high bytes.
